name: MonarchDashboardGrid
title: DashboardGrid
wrapsNative: VStack of HStack rows sized from onGeometryChange (widgets spanning columns); draggable(_:) and dropDestination(for:action:isTargeted:) in edit mode; Button with .buttonStyle(.monarch(.ghost, size: .sm)) for Move earlier and Move later
summary: The responsive grid a dashboard's widgets sit in: one column on phones, more on wide screens, widgets spanning columns, and an edit mode in which people rearrange widgets by dragging or with buttons.
whenToUse: On a home or dashboard screen made of several independent MonarchWidgets, especially when each person should be able to put the widgets they use most first.
whenNotToUse: For equal tiles without spans or stored layouts, use MonarchSortableGrid. For a single list of sections, use a VStack. For many items of the same kind, use a LazyVGrid.
api: init(_ items: [Item], layout: Binding<[Item.ID]>, itemLabel: KeyPath<Item, String>, span: ((Item) -> MonarchDashboardGridSpan)? = nil, columns: Int = 3, isEditing: Bool = false, labels: MonarchDashboardGridLabels = MonarchDashboardGridLabels(), onLayoutChange: (@MainActor (_ from: Int, _ to: Int) -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (Item) -> Content) where Item: Identifiable
enum MonarchDashboardGridSpan { case columns(Int), full; static let one, two }
struct MonarchDashboardGridLabels { var label, dragHint: String?; var moveEarlier, moveLater: (@Sendable (String) -> String)?; var moved, dropped: (@Sendable (String, Int, Int) -> String)? }

options.name: items
options.description: The widgets in their default order.

options.name: layout
options.description: The order of ids stored for this person; empty for the default order. Unknown ids are skipped and new items appended; the grid writes the new order after each move.

options.name: itemLabel
options.description: A widget's plain-text name, for the arrange bar, the button labels and the announcements.

options.name: span
options.description: The columns a widget spans on wide screens, clamped to the columns available. One by default.

options.name: columns
options.description: The columns from 1024 points of grid width, 1 to 4. From 640 points the grid has at most two, below it one.

options.name: isEditing
options.description: Shows an arrange bar on each widget with Move earlier and Move later, and makes the bars draggable.

options.name: onLayoutChange
options.description: Called after each finished move with the old and new index, for example to save the layout.

options.name: content
options.description: Draws a widget, usually a MonarchWidget.

states.name: viewing
states.description: The widgets in rows; one column on phones.

states.name: editing
states.description: Each widget has an arrange bar in the subtle background: a grip, its name, and Move earlier and Move later buttons, disabled at the ends.

states.name: drop target
states.description: While a bar is dragged over a widget, that widget has an accent outline.

appearance: Widgets sit with a 16-point gap. The arrange bar uses the subtle background role with muted text and grip; the move buttons are small ghost MonarchButtons; the drop outline uses the accent strong role at twice the hairline. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes come from these roles.
platformNotes: The web grid is a CSS grid with column spans; SwiftUI's LazyVGrid has no spans, so the iOS grid packs widgets into rows and sizes them from the measured width (it is not lazy; a dashboard has a few widgets). The web picks up a widget with Space and moves it with the arrow keys; on iOS the Move earlier and Move later buttons are the single-tap equivalent for touch, VoiceOver, Switch Control and keyboards, and dragging uses the system drag and drop. The web takes uncontrolled defaultLayout; on iOS the layout is a binding. The web widths are in rem of grid width (40rem, 64rem); iOS uses the 640 and 1024 point breakpoints. Android uses the same name and options. Several closures are optional (span, onLayoutChange). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is span.
accessibility: The grid is a container named "Dashboard".
In edit mode the bar reads the widget's name with the hint "Touch and hold, then drag to move."; its grip is hidden.
Move earlier and Move later are named with the widget ("Move Team load earlier"), have 44-point touch targets and are disabled at the ends.
Every move and drop is announced ("Team load moved to position 2 of 6.").
At the accessibility text sizes the grid has one column.
Moves animate with the motion tokens and are instant with Reduce Motion.
edgeCases: A stored layout with ids of removed widgets skips them; new widgets follow in their default order.
A widget whose span does not fit in what is left of a row starts the next row, leaving a gap.
In one column, spans have no effect and the move buttons point up and down; in several they point backward and forward and mirror right to left.
Drops from another grid or another app are ignored.
